name: United Space Coast Cables Inc
old_description: is a well established Electrical Contract Manufacturer with recognized knowledge and experience in the wire harness and cable assembly industry.
about:
United Space Coast Cables Inc. (USCC) operates from West Melbourne, Florida, where it has established itself as a lean contract manufacturer specializing in wire harness and cable assembly. The company's core management team brings over 100 years of combined experience in high‑technology manufacturing, though a founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

USCC produces custom cable assemblies and wire harnesses, offering engineering prototypes, first articles, and complex harness builds. The shop emphasizes in‑process inspection and testing, performing 100 % test and 100 % final inspection on every assembly. Its testing capabilities include patented graphic wiring displays that pinpoint faults instantly, with expandable test points up to 1,048 and cable length measurement up to 1,000 feet. The facility also measures resistance from 0.5 ohms to 10 megohms, checks embedded resistors and diode orientation, and generates high‑resolution graphic test documentation.

The company serves a broad spectrum of military, medical, and commercial markets. Its customer base includes organizations requiring high‑reliability interconnect solutions for defense, healthcare, and general industrial applications.

USCC positions its sole focus on wire harness manufacturing as a differentiator, noting that it has no proprietary products competing for production capacity. The firm highlights its commitment to on‑time delivery, comprehensive service, and a quality management system certified to ISO 9001:2015, with the stated goal of building partnerships by honoring commitments.

name: United Stretch Design Corp.
old_description: Manufacturing elastic and non-elastic cords, braids, ropes and tapes for unique and practical solutions.
about:
United Stretch Design Corp. operates from Hudson, Massachusetts, where it was founded in 1983 by Manuel P. Chaves. The company began as a braided-products specialist and has remained a domestic manufacturer of elastic and non‑elastic cords, braids, ropes, and tapes.

Its production capabilities include high‑speed braiding for flat elastic, shock cord, and a range of ropes from heavy‑duty marine lines to household utility cord. In‑house services cover custom labeling and spooling, custom colors and patterns, tie‑down and loop assemblies, calender finishing, polishing, cut‑to‑length cutting, tipping, and hanking. The facility runs industry‑high‑speed shock‑cord machines and works with synthetic, natural, and specialty fibers such as Dyneema.

The company serves automotive, marine, military, filtration, outdoor‑recreation, apparel, and general cord‑and‑rope markets worldwide. Customers range from OEMs needing mil‑spec 550 paracord to recreational brands requiring custom‑colored elastic webbing.

United Stretch Design emphasizes its "Made in America" heritage and a commitment to quality, delivery, and customer satisfaction. The firm highlights its ability to produce mil‑spec paracord and to tailor materials, colors, and assemblies to exact specifications.

name: Universal Pure - Meriden, CT
old_description: We are Universal Pure – the nation’s leading HPP provider, helping brands extend shelf life, protect consumers, and deliver clean-label products without heat or chemicals.
about:
Universal Pure operates its Meriden, Connecticut headquarters alongside a major processing facility in Lincoln, Nebraska. The company provides high pressure processing (HPP) and cold‑chain services to food and beverage brands across North America. A founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm’s core service is high pressure processing, a non‑thermal pasteurization method that uses cold water and extreme pressure to inactivate pathogens while preserving nutrition, taste, and texture. Universal Pure runs the largest network of HPP facilities in North America, equipped with both Avure and Hiperbaric presses. In Lincoln, the site offers blast freezing, static freezing, and refrigerated storage with USDA licensing, FDA registration, and SQF Level III certification. Value‑added services include repackaging, kitting, labeling, air and water tempering, code‑date ink jetting, netting, inventory management, and full‑load or LTL logistics. An in‑house team of 18 engineers and technicians supports equipment uptime, process validation, and packaging optimization.

Customers span protein processors, beverage makers, dip and spread producers, dairy and cheese manufacturers, and pet‑food brands. The company serves food manufacturers, beverage manufacturers, grocery and retail chains, food‑service operators, warehouse clubs, and direct‑to‑consumer brands. A published case study details work with Chairman’s Foods, a fresh‑salad and refrigerated‑food producer that used HPP to transition a chicken casserole from frozen to fresh.

Universal Pure positions its scale and engineering depth as differentiators: the multi‑site footprint allows load balancing across presses, the internal engineering group drives lower cost‑per‑cycle, and SQF Level III certification underpins a validation‑support program for partners. The company states its mission is to help brands achieve cleaner labels, longer shelf life, and reduced food waste without heat or chemical preservatives.
